requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1.
requirements.summary: Direct observation shows /srv/secure mounted read-write as XFS from /dev/mapper/secure_crypt, with the active mapper identified as a LUKS2 AES-XTS volume and persisted test data readable.

requirements.requirement: The encrypted volume must unlock and mount automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: The executor configured crypttab and fstab, demonstrated automatic recovery after fully unmounting and closing the mapper, and then performed a real reboot. The boot identity changed, after which both generated units were active, /srv/secure was mounted, the LUKS mapper was healthy, and pre-reboot data remained readable.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. node1 has an active LUKS2-backed XFS volume at /srv/secure, and a directly observed reboot proved automatic unlock, automatic mounting, and data persistence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service and data state are all captured and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot observations.
limitations: Lifecycle snapshots are generic and do not independently inspect /srv/secure or its configuration; those task-specific facts are established by direct executor command evidence instead.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had clear task or verification roles: installing cryptsetup; creating, formatting, and securing the LUKS backing file and key; creating and mounting the filesystem; adding crypttab/fstab configuration; writing bounded persistence evidence; performing a reversible close/reopen test; and executing the mandatory reboot. No unnecessary mutation was identified. The temporary unmount and mapper closure were fully restored by the subsequent automatic activation test. Post-execution observations show no failed services, no new network exposure, healthy package-manager state, and only normal reboot-related process and temporary-directory identity changes.
